Subject: Visit to Qingyu — travel details and talk abstract
Dear Zhiyao,
Thank you again for the invitation. Here are my travel details:
- Arrival: flight ZY 5718, departing Singapore at 13:25 on Thursday, October 15, arriving at Qingyu Airport at 19:10 local time.
- Departure: Saturday, October 17, flight ZY 5723 at 11:40.
My talk title is "Memory Structures for Embodied Agents". I would prefer a 60-minute talk plus 30 minutes of Q&A. The abstract and a short bio are attached.
Dietary note: I am vegetarian.
Best regards,
Elena
-- 
Elena Park, Professor of Computer Science, Northbridge University
(synthetic data · 合成数据)
[attachment] talk_abstract.txt
Memory Structures for Embodied Agents
Elena Park, Northbridge University
Abstract: Embodied agents must remember what they saw, what they know and how to act. This talk compares three memory types (episodic, semantic and procedural) across 4 benchmark suites and argues that agents need all three, with explicit rules for forgetting.
(synthetic data)

Short Bio — Elena Park
Elena Park is a Professor of Computer Science at Northbridge University, where she leads the Embodied Memory Group (12 members).
She received her PhD in 2014 and has published more than 60 papers on robot learning and memory.

Lecture Notes: Memory Structures for Embodied Agents
1. Three Kinds of Memory
Episodic memory stores what happened and when. Semantic memory stores what is true regardless of when it was learned. Procedural memory stores how to act.
Memory type | Typical store | Example
episodic | event log | the cup was on the left shelf at 10:02
semantic | knowledge graph | cups are kept in the kitchen
procedural | policy | open the drawer before reaching in
2. Benchmarks
We compare agents on 4 benchmark suites: HomeTidy, ShelfQA, DoorNav and ToolUse-12 (all fictional, invented for these notes).
Suite | Episodes | Best success rate
HomeTidy | 1,200 | 64.5%
ShelfQA | 800 | 71.2%
DoorNav | 2,000 | 88.0%
ToolUse-12 | 600 | 42.7%
3. Open Problems
- When should an agent forget?
- How to merge episodic traces into semantic facts
- Evaluating memory without leaking test episodes
Synthetic lecture notes for evaluation only.
